facts: These appeals arise out of orders passed in petitions moved before the High Court of Orissa challenging the scheme adopted by the Government of Orissa for sale of Kendu leaves.
Kendu tree is a wild growth.
To regulate the trade in Kendu leaves the State of Orissa has adopted diverse executive, and legislative measures.

A trader in Kendu leaves challenged the validity of the Act and the Order before the High Court of Orissa on the plea that the State Legislature was incompetent to enact the Act and that in any event the Act and the Order infringed the guarantee of fundamental freedom to carry on business under Art. 19(1)(g) of the Constitution.
The main purpose of the Order was to prevent indiscriminate and unrestricted competition in the trade in Kendu leaves and to protect the growers and pluckers from exploitation.
issues: Whether the State Legislature was competent to enact the Act
Whether the Act and the Order infringed the guarantee of fundamental freedom to carry on business under Art. 19(1)(g) of the Constitution
petitioner_arguments: The State Legislature was incompetent to enact the Act
The Act and the Order infringed the guarantee of fundamental freedom to carry on business under Art. 19(1)(g) of the Constitution
respondent_arguments: The main purpose of the Order was to prevent indiscriminate and unrestricted competition in the trade in Kendu leaves and to protect the growers and pluckers from exploitation
The fixation of prices prescribed by S. 4 was reasonable and in the 'interest of the general public both under Art. 19(5) and Art. 19(6) and S. 4 of the Act was on that account valid
court_reasoning: The Orissa Kendu (Control of Trade) Act, 1961, was a valid piece of legislation
Creation of a State monopoly in Kendu leaves was protected by Art. 19(6) as amended by the Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951
Fixation of prices prescribed by S. 4 was reasonable and in the 'interest of the general public both under Art. 19(5) and Art. 19(6) and S. 4 of the Act was on that account valid
holding: The State Government was incompetent to implement the provisions of the Act through the Agents appointed under those agreements

The new scheme adopted by the State Government for offering to enter into agreements for advance purchases of Kendu leaves by private negotiation was a colourable device to make it appear constitutional and permissible under Art. 19(6) (ii) of the Constitution
